name: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Land area 1,122,135 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2, mid); high is surface area incl. inland water 1,129,819 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 135,472,051). Low allows for census uncertainty; high adds one year of growth to 2026 (~2.6%/yr).

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.485 as quoted: 503,000 active (mid; reflects the post-2023 integration of regional special forces and wartime recruitment). CIA Factbook 2025: "150-300,000"; World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 138,000 (2020). Range spans all; grade C because estimates differ by a factor of three.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. IISS lists no organised reserve; former regional special forces, demobilised Tigray-war veterans and militias are a large informal pool. Callups are legal and compulsory (CIA Factbook 2025).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 503,000 (IISS 2026) minus infantry P roles (90,000 + 280,000) = 133,000: armour/artillery crews, air force, logistics, staff, Defence Cyber directorate.

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy: callups are compulsory when ordered and the 2021 national call raised hundreds of thousands, but arms and logistics limit mass mobilization. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Infantry of the mechanised divisions (~one per regional command in IISS 2009-era structure) after Tigray-war expansion. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.5: conscript-like volunteers with extensive combat experience (Tigray 2020-22, Fano, OLA).

count.note: Educated guess. Infantry divisions and integrated former regional special forces; bulk of the 503,000 (IISS 2026).

training.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: rapid wartime expansion diluted training.

count.note: MBT list: T-55 170 + T-62 50 + T-72 ~250 = ~470 (mid). Army equipment list totals 1,879 (T-72 569, T-54/55 1,190, T-62 120) are cumulative deliveries; high ~1,000 allows for stored hulls. Low reflects Tigray-war losses (2020-22).

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: T-55/T-62 obsolete; T-72UA1/T-72B era-typical for the region.

count.note: Army list: BMP-1 337 + BTR-60 560 + Type 92 420 + WZ-523 270 + ZSD-89 10 + Bastion 12 + Gaia Thunder 400+ + Calidus MCAV-20 400+ = ~2,400 (high, cumulative deliveries). IISS Military Balance 2012 as quoted on the Ethiopian Army article: ~450 BRDM/BMP/BTR/Type 89 in service. Mid ~1,000 allows for the 2020s IMV deliveries.

Army list tubes/launchers: 2S1 82 + 2S19 160 + PLZ-45 158 + SH-15 342 + BM-21 500 + Type 63 500+ + PHL-03 40 + M-46 600 + M-30 464 + D-30 309 = ~3,150 (high ~3,500 with mortars excluded). These are cumulative and partly inflated; mid ~900 is an educated judgement after war losses (grade C).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: SH-15/PLZ-45/2S19 modern, rest towed Soviet guns.

count.note: Air Force inventory: Su-27SK 16 + Su-30K 6 + Su-35 12 (Bloomberg-reported delivery; unconfirmed by World Air Forces) = 34 (high). Mid assumes ~half of the Su-35 report is real or serviceable.
MiG-23BN 9 + Su-25 3 = 12. Yak-130 (6) trainers not counted.
World Air Forces 2026 as quoted: Mi-8/17 15 + Mi-35 7 + Alouette III 3, plus Army UH-1 8 = 33.

TB2 4 + Wing Loong II 2 + Akinci (few, 2024) + Mohajer-6 (unknown) + Orion-E (2026, unknown). Counts largely unpublished; mid is an estimate. Drones were decisive in the 2021 counter-offensive (Al Jazeera via the EAF article).

Launcher counts converted at ~4-6 per battery (SOURCES.md): S-75M3 89 ~15, S-125 40 ~8, Pantsir-S1 61 ~10, HQ-64 12 ~2, SPYDER 26 ~4, ZSU-23-4 60 ~10 = ~49 (S-400 4 batteries on order not counted). List figures may be cumulative; range 20-60.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: Pantsir/SPYDER modern, S-75/S-125 obsolete.

count.note: Educated guess. DF-12/M20 tactical ballistic missiles reported purchased (Army list says quantity unknown); launcher count unknown. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Ethiopian_Army)

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: experienced general staff (Tigray war 2020-22 counter-offensive, drone integration), politicised command.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: national army with ethnic fault lines (Tigrayan purge 2020, Amhara Fano defections 2023).

morale.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: war-weariness from multiple internal conflicts.

weapons.note: Anchor 8-9: Soviet-era bulk with modern pieces (Pantsir, SH-15, UCAVs, DF-12).

ships.note: Anchor 0: no naval force. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: 7.5 -> 0, no naval force in service: the navy re-established in 2019 has no operational vessels.

fortification.note: Anchor 8-9: field works; partial SAM cover of Addis Ababa.

logistics.note: Anchor 8: motor transport, Addis-Djibouti railway, 3 Il-76.

isr.note: Anchor 9: MALE UCAV ISR (Akinci, Wing Loong II), no military satellites (ET-RSS-1 is civil).

cyber.note: Anchor 9 minus: Defence Cyber Main Directorate, INSA.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 335,624,139,356 2011 int$ / population 135,472,051 = 2,477. Range +/-15%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 419,268,131,613 x 0.8005 = 335,624,139,356 2011 int$. Range +/-15%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 0.49% of GDP in 2025. The official figure likely understates wartime spending (Tigray war, Fano/OLA COIN); high 1.5% is an educated allowance.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and mining/oil where present) 27.8% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). +/-2 points.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.31. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ETH/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 60.14% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.87 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.87-0.88). Mid 1 - 0.601/0.87 = 0.31. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.87 = 0.17. High: s 0.88 = 0.32. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 87% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Large subsistence agriculture, recurring food aid needs; small marketable surplus. Not from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 67,876,104 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share aged 15-19 11.059% / 5 = 1,501,322. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10%.

artillery.note: Educated guess. Gafat Armament Engineering Complex and Bishoftu Automotive overhaul and assemble guns, MRLs and armoured vehicles. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Ethiopian_Army)

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Bishoftu Automotive licence assembly. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Ethiopian_Army)

roadKm.note: Road list (2018): 120,171 km total incl. rural roads (high). Low is the ~16,000 km of asphalt. Mid is the geometric mean of the two, a judgment value.

railKm.note: asOf 2018: 754 route-km (World Bank IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). CIA Factbook 659 km (2017) spans the range. Addis Ababa-Djibouti standard-gauge electric line is the only railway.

majorPorts.note: Landlocked; trade goes through Djibouti (about 90%), Berbera and Lamu.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. CIA Factbook: 12 ships (10 general cargo, 2 tankers) under Ethiopian Shipping and Logistics Services, 2023; tonnage not in the merchant list. (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/africa/et.json)

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Truck sustainment over long mountain roads; demonstrated deep advances in 2021-22.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Ethiopia has Africa's largest equine herd (donkeys, mules, horses); pack animals used in highland operations. Not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.3: mountainous highland plateau, harsh terrain and climate for invaders, strategic depth and strong national defence tradition (Adwa 1896).

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data, 2026 order of battle. Thin and contradictory data: IISS 2026 (as quoted) puts active strength at 503,000 versus 150-300,000 (CIA) and 138,000 (World Bank 2020); equipment lists on Wikipedia mix cumulative deliveries with holdings and are grade C. Internal conflicts ongoing (Fano in Amhara, OLA in Oromia; Pretoria agreement with TPLF 2022 fragile) and tension with Eritrea over sea access. Population convention: everything inside ne:ETH. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011 (+/-15%). No sea-going navy. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Regional police special forces excluded.
